findings.title: Unencrypted Storage of Personal Biometric Baselines at Rest
findings.description: Astronaut personal health baselines containing individualized longitudinal telemetry, quantiles, and historical session logs are stored in plaintext SQLite on the local edge filesystem.
findings.impact: Unauthorized physical or host-level access to the edge device could leak sensitive astronaut physiological profiles.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SQLCipher or AES-256 GCM envelope encryption for biometric database tables prior to spaceflight deployment.

findings.title: Lack of Telemetry Ingestion Cryptographic Signing / Authentication
findings.description: Session inputs accept `astronaut_id` and telemetry features via Pydantic schemas without HMAC or digital signature verification.
findings.impact: An adversary on the local vehicle bus could forge telemetry sessions attributed to an astronaut, leading to baseline corruption if not caught by sanity boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Require cryptographic token or sensor enclave signature on telemetry ingestion sessions.

findings.title: Unbounded In-Memory Historical Observation Buffer in Updates
findings.description: Takes `all_historical_sessions: List[ObservationSession]` in memory. In an ultra-long mission (e.g. Mars 3-year transit), loading tens of thousands of sessions could cause edge OOM.
findings.impact: Denial of service on memory-constrained flight computer.
findings.recommendation: Implement streaming / windowed rolling recalculation or incremental Welford/P-Square quantile estimation.

findings.title: Active Pre-Release Python Runtime (3.10.0rc2)
findings.description: Environment executes on Python 3.10.0rc2, an unpatched pre-release candidate.
findings.impact: Potential unpatched CPython bugs or ABI differences.
findings.recommendation: Deploy on official stable release (e.g., Python 3.10.14+ or 3.11/3.12) with frozen wheels.
